question: Do correct positions produce a repeatable positive contribution compared with no positions at 2048 neurons?
dataset: Same Stringer MP019 recording; reused chronological validation/test segments, explicitly exploratory
budget: Exactly36 new fits plus18 reused matching fits:54 fits,18 matched triples; do not extend contingent on outcome
primary_contrast: MSE(no positions)-MSE(real positions); positive means real positions help
secondary_contrast: MSE(shuffled positions)-MSE(real positions); positive favors the true cell-position mapping over arbitrary fixed identifiers
reporting: report old18,new36,combined54 and old/new neuron pools separately; count paired wins and pool-level means; show validation and test and raw/bounded MSE; do not choose individual favorable seeds
design: unchanged architecture, neuron selection algorithm, normalization, coordinate shuffle rule, training budget and split from density study; six pools of2048 cells with three optimizer seeds each
earlier_consistency_gate: retain all-pool consistency rule: real coordinates must beat each control in every pool mean as well as overall; evaluate none-only contribution and geometry contribution separately
uncertainty: exploratory crossed resampling of neuron pools, training-seed blocks, and contiguous test-time blocks;2000 resamples,100-bin circular blocks; same sampled units across conditions; conditional on this single recording, not animal-level significance
